newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower on Monday ending a three-day rally on what traders said was a technical correction.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.32 percent, or 0.83 points, to 254.86 on all-share turnover of 102 million shekels against 130 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.45 percent lower at 263.86.

"The Maof index rose sharply from 250 in only three sessions and all the technical indicators show that it needs to gain strength before it breaks through the 265 level," said Baruch Glicksberg at Clal Insurance.
Shahar Gazit at Batucha Securities and Investment said that the main reason for the decline was profit taking.
"The market rose sharply and now it's time for a technical correction. Investors are also waiting for fresh news before they decide on further investments," Gazit said.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu arrived in Washington on Monday for talks with U.S. President Bill Clinton on rescuing Middle East peace moves.

"The market is in a holding pattern and investors wait to see what will be the outcome of Netanyahu's trip to Washington. The market is looking now for direction and it's difficult to say where it is going," Glicksberg added.
Netanyahu hopes to get Clinton behind his offer to seal a final peace with the PLO in six months ending, if necessary, with an intensive U.S.-Israeli-PLO summit.

Israel Discount Bank gained 0.5 percent to 350 agorot. MI Holdings, the government company in charge of privatising Israel's banks, said on Monday that the institutional tranche of the Discount's share and warrants offering was 1.7 times oversubscribed.

The most active shares were Bank Hapoalim, which fell 1.0 percent to 699 agorot on volume of 3.7 million shekels; Bank Leumi, which lost 1.75 percent to 568 on turnover of 3.5 million shekels; and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which rose 0.75 percent to 18,896 agorot on turnover of 3.3 million shekels.
